article.title: Dinner for the Team
article.content:
After a football match, Daniel offered to make dinner for three teammates. He chose vegetable pasta because it seemed simple. Before shopping, he sent a message asking what everyone could eat. One friend could not eat cheese, so Daniel planned to serve it in a separate bowl.

At the shop, Daniel discovered that tomatoes were more expensive than usual. He bought a tin of tomatoes instead of fresh ones and stayed within his budget. He prepared the sauce early, but waited until his friends arrived to cook the pasta. That way, it would not become too soft. Everyone enjoyed the meal. Daniel thought the most useful part of cooking was not following a difficult recipe, but making a plan that worked for his guests.
article.translation:
一场足球比赛后，丹尼尔提出给三位队友做晚饭。他选择了看起来简单的蔬菜意面。购物前，他发消息询问大家能吃什么。一位朋友不能吃奶酪，于是他打算把奶酪单独盛在一个碗里。

到商店后，丹尼尔发现西红柿比平时贵。他用罐装番茄代替新鲜西红柿，没有超出预算。他提前做好酱汁，等朋友到达后才煮面，以免面条太软。大家都喜欢这顿饭。丹尼尔觉得，做饭最有用的部分不是照着复杂食谱操作，而是制定适合客人的计划。

questions.prompt: Why did Daniel serve cheese separately?
options: One friend could not eat it
He wanted to keep it for breakfast
questions.explanation: 第一段明确指出一位朋友不能吃奶酪，因此要分开盛。

questions.prompt: How did Daniel stay within his budget?
options: He asked his friends to pay
questions.explanation: 新鲜西红柿贵，他改买罐装番茄，从而控制了花费。

questions.prompt: Why did he wait to cook the pasta?
options: He did not have a pot
He wanted it to keep a good texture
His friends wanted to cook everything
questions.explanation: 文中说“That way, it would not become too soft”，即避免面条太软。
